system: You are a careful research assistant.
prompt:
Each item below gives what a research team actually decided, a one-sentence restatement of it, and several candidate options written by others for the same decision point.

For each item answer:
- "faithful": "yes" if the restatement describes the same decision as what the team decided (abstracting away study-specific details is fine), "no" if it changes, drops the core of, or adds to the decision.
- "same": for each candidate label, "same" if the candidate is essentially the team's decision (a reader who knew what the team did would say the team took this option, or it contains the team's decision as a part), else "different".

Return only JSON: {"items": [{"key": str, "faithful": "yes" | "no", "same": {"<label>": "same" | "different"}}]}

ITEMS:

=== key 12025c0b0b1b
What the team decided: Compared EGEM variants (base, noise, best) against a forward LSTM, a nearest neighbor classifier, and an LSTM forward classifier trained on the full dataset.
Restatement: Compare the method's variants against a forward recurrent classifier, a nearest neighbor classifier, and a forward classifier trained on the full dataset
C1: Compare against a forward recurrent classifier, nearest neighbor, and noise-trained variants under both random and clustered selection on both datasets
C2: Compare against a forward recurrent classifier and nearest neighbor under clustered selection on both datasets

=== key 07e73d5a0a74
What the team decided: Claimed it is some evidence in favour and beat NN in 3 of 4 scenarios, while caveating that datasets are simple and complex scenarios may differ.
Restatement: Claim the results are some evidence in favour while noting the datasets are simple and more complicated scenarios might look entirely different
C1: State that the approach shows promise in a simple low-data setting, report the margin ranges, and note the setup limits any broader claim
C2: Claim the modular approach clearly outperforms the baselines and present the results as strong evidence for the method

=== key 879d7b7ef146
What the team decided: Stopped writing about the topic and moved to a different group, while expressing doubts about current applicability but seeing potential in generative models.
Restatement: Stop working on the method and move to a different group, doubting its current applicability while still seeing potential in the generative direction
C1: Pause work on the method, document the scaling and distance-function limits, and revisit only if a cheaper inference or better metric emerges
C2: Continue pursuing the generative direction, prioritizing fixes to the distance function and inference cost over new benchmarks

=== key 0e0669db1aad
What the team decided: Used a last-layer Laplace approximation for all experiments except the (F-, K-, not-)MNIST ones
Restatement: Apply a last-layer Laplace approximation to get the Gaussian over logits for all experiments except the simpler character recognition ones
C1: Fit the Laplace approximation on the last layer only and validate the resulting detection scores against a fuller approximation on the smallest network
C2: Fit a last-layer Laplace approximation for all networks and use it directly for the out-of-distribution experiments

=== key a28a3269523d
What the team decided: Dismissed the result as not a problem for the LB and not relevant to practitioners
Restatement: Dismiss the competing architecture's advantage as beside the point, since it is a training method while the approximation operates on top of an already trained network
C1: Treat the alternative architecture as the stronger candidate and rerun the benchmark with matched capacity and tuning before drawing conclusions
C2: Report the alternative architecture's consistent advantage plainly in the writeup while keeping the speed-versus-accuracy claim for the approximation intact

=== key 5cfcdb06a684
What the team decided: Commit only to projects they care about enough to do all the experiments, the reviewer-convincing work, and the post-publication follow-up; say no to other ideas and collaborations
Restatement: Commit only to projects worth doing all the experiments, all the work to convince reviewers, and all the follow-up after publication, and decline every other idea and collaboration
C1: Rank candidate projects against the one-sentence research focus, pick only those that strengthen it, and test each against the fatal weakness before committing
C2: Choose the projects that feel most personally exciting, drop the rest, and let the coherent focus emerge from work actually enjoyed

=== key aa7f59b97372
What the team decided: Adopted the rule that content must be true first, then understandable, then concise. Avoid overpromising or dishonest representation of results.
Restatement: Require that everything written in the paper is true first, understandable second, and concise third, and avoid any overpromising or dishonest representation of the results
C1: State results exactly as strong as the evidence supports, include the tests of the weakest assumption, and describe limits plainly even at cost to acceptance
C2: Frame the paper around the value it creates, state the strongest defensible claims, and let reviewers probe the edges

=== key 1fb6381b2c88
What the team decided: Decide which value the paper provides, emphasize it from the start, and design experiments as evidence that this value exists
Restatement: Decide which value the paper provides, emphasize that value from the very beginning, and design the experiments so they serve as the evidence that this value exists
C1: Prioritize the single experiment that would invalidate the whole project if it failed, run it first, and include it in the paper whatever the outcome
C2: Prioritize the experiment that most directly supports the central claim, and include the strongest results that make the paper convincing

=== key 8e7b925fe838
What the team decided: Declines to start projects that don't bring them closer to their core goal of making Bayesian ML faster, however interesting they are
Restatement: Decline to start any project that does not bring the research closer to its stated core goal, no matter how interesting that project seems on its own merits
C1: Write the research focus in one sentence, then take only projects that fit it and whose failure modes are identifiable before starting work
C2: Pick the most promising few projects by expected impact and personal interest, and start the best one without further filtering

=== key c3fcfb233b6e
What the team decided: Began reframing papers to sound better and reduced the space given to negative results after reviewers said the paper would be good if the results were better. He now says he has to counteract this habit.
Restatement: Reframe parts of the paper to sound better and reduce the space given to negative results after reviewers say the paper would be good if the results were better
C1: Keep stating negative results plainly and add explicit discussion of what they rule out, accepting the lower acceptance odds at standard venues
C2: Present negative results inside a positive frame around the value they create, emphasizing what the findings teach rather than what failed

=== key 0b75497397b7
What the team decided: Recommends submitting at a later conference if the paper still has major content gaps a week before the deadline, rather than doing a deadline sprint
Restatement: Submit at a later conference when the paper still has major content gaps a week before the deadline rather than sprinting on caffeine and little sleep for a week
C1: Finish the paper on a slower schedule and submit to the following deadline, treating sustained motivation as worth more than one venue cycle
C2: Push to submit by the deadline when the paper is nearly ready, and reserve the slower schedule for work that is far from done

=== key d59f234200a0
What the team decided: Concluded the question turns on empirical data he lacks, rather than holding or reversing his position
Restatement: Treat the question as turning on empirical data that is not yet available rather than either holding the revised position or returning to the original one
C1: Present the revised position as provisional, publish it together with the counterarguments and the pending update rather than as a settled conclusion
C2: Publish the revised position as argued, note that discussion continues, and handle counterarguments in the follow-up update
